data.title: Social Proof
data.tagline: Support a product claim with evidence from real use
data.description: Social proof can include customer logos, measured results, reviews, certifications, or case studies. Choose evidence that supports the claim next to it and state the source or context. A wall of unverified logos is weaker than one relevant, specific example.

use: Share a measured result with context
Link to a full case study
Display a relevant certification or review source
avoid: Use logos without permission or explanation
Show numbers with no source, period, or definition
Place unrelated awards beside a product claim
Repeat generic praise instead of giving evidence

lessonPractice.title: A site wants customer logos and Used by 100,000 teams, but the count is estimated and some logos lack display permission. What should happen?

options.label: Show only authorized assets and verifiable data, with date, definition, and source
options.feedback: Social proof derives value from credible external evidence. Permission and measurement notes explain what that evidence represents.

options.label: Publish recognizable customer logos first and request permission after the site launches
options.feedback: Unauthorized marks cannot serve as trustworthy evidence, and publishing first creates brand and factual risk.

options.label: Round the estimate to 100,000+ and omit its source as long as the number looks prominent
options.feedback: A number without audience, time, or source cannot be verified, and prominence amplifies the credibility problem.

data.agentPrompt: Audit the site's social proof: record permission status for every customer logo and add audience, date, and source to each metric. Remove anything unverifiable, do not recolor marks or invent quotes, and keep only evidence-backed customers, reviews, and data.
